title: Cape to Cairo — the great journey
pill: ★ CAPE TO CAIRO · THE GREAT JOURNEY
h1: Cape to Cairo — rail, wings & the Nile
sub: Six legs, one continent — the great train to the Indian Ocean, flights where no rails run, and a cruise down the Nile. Tap a leg to ride it.
cap: Modelled on the real Cape-to-Cairo luxury departures (32 days · from ±US$50 000 pp · the train alone from ±US$16 500). The rails end at Dar es Salaam — flown legs shown dashed, as every real operator flies them. Real cities shown for bearing; trains, stays & food generic (SO-1b). A demo a real tour operator could publish as their own — free to claim and replace with their product. AI imagery.
route_summary: Whole route · 6 legs · ~12 000 km · rails to the Indian Ocean, wings over the Rift, the Nile home. Benchmark: the real thing runs 32 days from ±US$50 000 pp.  Tap a leg to ride it.

days.title: Table Mountain to the Karoo
days.summary: Out of the Cape through the winelands and up onto a high, dry plateau of endless sky.

stops.name: Cape Town · the platform
stops.blurb: Table Mountain filling the window, brass, teak and a station clock — the journey starts formally.

stops.name: Cape Malay farewell lunch
stops.blurb: Spiced mince baked under savoury custard with yellow rice, then syrup-soaked plaited doughnuts with coconut.

stops.name: Through the winelands
stops.blurb: Whitewashed gables, vineyards in rows, and a wall of blue mountains the train has to find a way through.

stops.name: Victorian halt on the plateau
stops.blurb: A perfectly preserved railway village on the empty Karoo — gaslamps, a double-storey verandah, one street.

stops.name: First night in the sleeper
stops.blurb: Berth made up while you dine; the rhythm of rail joints and a lit lamp somewhere far out on the plain.

stops.name: Roosterkoek at the halt
stops.blurb: Griddle bread off the coals at a Victorian siding — split, buttered and eaten hot with apricot jam.

days.title: Karoo to the diamond city
days.summary: Across the great dry interior to the city built beside the largest hand-dug hole on earth.

stops.name: Dawn on the Karoo
stops.blurb: Pink light on flat-topped hills, windmills, sheep, and not one other vehicle.

stops.name: Karoo lamb, slow-roasted
stops.blurb: Lamb raised on wild aromatic scrub, so the meat arrives pre-seasoned — served pink with pumpkin fritters.

stops.name: The Big Hole
stops.blurb: A 200 m crater dug by hand by fifty thousand men with picks and buckets, now filled with green water.

stops.name: Highveld grassland
stops.blurb: Grass to the horizon in every direction, thunderheads stacking up in the afternoon.

stops.name: Second night, rolling north
stops.blurb: Dinner in the dining car under lamplight, then the long climb onto the highveld in the dark.

stops.name: Potjie under the stars
stops.blurb: Lamb, potatoes and sweet wine simmered for hours in a three-legged pot beside the line, under a sky thick with stars.

days.title: Highveld to the great falls
days.summary: North through the jacaranda capital, over the border, to the largest curtain of falling water on earth.

stops.name: Jacaranda capital
stops.blurb: Purple streets in spring, union buildings on the ridge, and the last big-city platform for a while.

stops.name: Biltong & braai on board
stops.blurb: Air-dried spiced beef sliced thin as a snack, then flame-grilled steak and coiled farm sausage for dinner.

stops.name: The smoke that thunders
stops.blurb: A kilometre-wide curtain dropping 100 m into a gorge; the spray column is visible 50 km away.

stops.name: The bridge over the gorge
stops.blurb: A 1905 steel arch spanning the chasm — the original dream of this whole railway, and the point it stalled.

stops.name: Colonial hotel by the falls
stops.blurb: Verandahs, ceiling fans, high tea, warthogs on the lawn and permanent thunder in the background.

stops.name: Zambezi bream by the river
stops.blurb: Whole bream off the coals at the water's edge, lemon-buttered, with the spray of the falls drifting over.

days.title: Across the plateau to the ocean
days.summary: The long haul east — miombo woodland, escarpment and a game park the line runs straight through. Journey's end for the rails: no railway runs north of Dar es Salaam.

stops.name: Onto the long line
stops.blurb: The famous cross-continental service: two nights, one train, minimal fuss.

stops.name: Game from the window
stops.blurb: The line runs through a national park — giraffe, elephant and buffalo from the dining-car window at walking pace.

stops.name: Grilled meat & maize
stops.blurb: Charcoal-grilled goat and beef with stiff maize porridge and a fierce tomato-chilli relish, eaten with hands.

stops.name: Spice port on the ocean
stops.blurb: Indian Ocean harbour thick with the smell of clove, cardamom and cinnamon from the islands offshore.

stops.name: Harbour-side rooms
stops.blurb: Carved doors, a courtyard, call to prayer at dusk and dhows on the water at first light.

stops.name: Chai na mandazi at dawn
stops.blurb: Sweet, gingery tea and warm fried dough as the miombo woodland slides past — Tanzania's answer to breakfast in bed.

days.title: Where the rails end — by air
days.summary: The railway stops at the Indian Ocean, so the journey grows wings — over the crater highlands, the Great Migration, a gorilla forest and the roof of Ethiopia, landing back on the Nile at Aswan. Sudan is overflown, as on every real departure.

stops.name: Ngorongoro Crater rim
stops.blurb: Sundowners on the lip of the world's largest unbroken caldera, the game grazing two thousand feet below.

stops.name: Serengeti · the Great Migration
stops.blurb: A million wildebeest and zebra on the move — often called the greatest show on earth.

stops.name: Gorillas of the Volcanoes
stops.blurb: One quiet hour with a mountain gorilla family in the bamboo forests of Rwanda.

stops.name: Injera in Addis Ababa
stops.blurb: Sour flatbread piled with spiced stews and lentils, eaten by hand from one shared platter.

stops.name: Coffee, born in Ethiopia
stops.blurb: The ceremony: green beans roasted at your feet, pounded, brewed three times — coffee in the country that gave it to the world.

stops.name: Lalibela, carved from rock
stops.blurb: Eleven medieval churches chiselled straight down into the mountain, still in daily use.

stops.name: Abu Simbel colossi
stops.blurb: Ramses II at twenty metres, rescued stone by stone above Lake Nasser.

days.title: Aswan to the Pyramids
days.summary: A slow cruise between temple banks from Aswan to Luxor, then the night sleeper into Cairo and the oldest tourist attraction on earth.

stops.name: Casting off at Aswan
stops.blurb: Three slow nights on the river — dinner on deck as the palms slide by and the banks turn copper.

stops.name: Temple city at dawn
stops.blurb: Avenues of stone rams, hypostyle halls of vast painted columns, cut sharp by early light.

stops.name: Rice, lentils & fried onion
stops.blurb: The great street dish — rice, lentils and macaroni under spiced tomato sauce, vinegar and crisp onions.

stops.name: The green Nile valley
stops.blurb: A ribbon of intense green a few kilometres wide with hard desert on both edges — the whole country in one view.

stops.name: Mint tea in sight of the tombs
stops.blurb: Sweet mint tea on a rooftop with the three pyramids filling the skyline behind the cups.

stops.name: The night sleeper to Cairo
stops.blurb: Boarding at dusk with the river turning copper — dinner served in the cabin as the palms slide by.

stops.name: Journey's end · Cairo
stops.blurb: Ten thousand kilometres, one continent, and a last look back down the line from the Giza plateau.

heritage: The island prison where Nelson Mandela spent 18 years.
Ramses II's rock temples, moved block by block above the rising lake.
The greatest temple complex of the ancient world.
The last surviving wonder of the ancient world, at the end of the line.
